extraction_text: The armies of the Kauravas and Pandavas meet for battle, creating a tremendous noise.

attributes.description: The sound of warriors, conches, drums, elephants, chariots, and horses fills the air, shaking the earth and sky. The armies are described as shining with gold and flags.

extraction_text: The Kaurava army, led by Bhishma, is described in detail with its formations and key protectors.

attributes.description: Bhishma is at the front. Duryodhana, Duhshasana, Durmukha, and Durmarsha protect him from behind. Other warriors and armies from various regions, including 20,000 chariots, 10,000 elephants, 600,000 soldiers protecting wheels and elephant legs, and hundreds of thousands of infantry, form the eleven Akshauhinis of the Kaurava army. It is compared to the Ganga river splitting from the Yamuna.

extraction_text: King Dhritarashtra, through Sanjaya, questions how the smaller Pandava army can face the massive Kaurava formation led by the expert Bhishma.

attributes.description: Dhritarashtra asks Sanjaya how Yudhishthira, with his smaller army, can possibly face the eleven Akshauhinis of the Kaurava army, which is led by the supremely knowledgeable Bhishma.

extraction_text: Yudhishthira, seeing the Kaurava formation, advises Arjuna to arrange their smaller army in a concentrated needle-point formation (Suchimukha Vyuha) as prescribed by the sage Brihaspati.

attributes.description: Yudhishthira, the Dharma King, observes the enemy formation and tells Arjuna that since their army is the minority, they should deploy it in a tight, concentrated needle-point array as advised by the sage Brihaspati for a smaller force fighting a larger one.

extraction_text: Arjuna responds that he will arrange the Pandava army in the formidable Vajra (Thunderbolt) formation, also known as the Achala (Immovable) formation, as arranged by Indra.

attributes.description: Arjuna tells Yudhishthira that he will deploy their army in the difficult-to-defeat Vajra Vyuha (Thunderbolt formation), which is the array arranged by the wielder of the thunderbolt, Indra. This introduces a divine/supernatural element to the military strategy.
